balance_notes: GDD 2.3.5, full hold doubles the ship, fixed against the flown per-slot mass rather than my own compactor-case arithmetic. The audit measured 232.96 kg per crushed slot across the shipping slice, so 6 base slots is 1,397.8 kg. dry_mass_kg moves 850 to 1,350 and the ratio becomes (1350 + 1397.8) / 1350 = 2747.8 / 1350 = 2.035x, inside the 1.75-2.25 window with room on both sides. I moved dry mass and not base_slots: 6 slots is on screen in the GDD 2.2 walkthrough ('Cargo reads 4 of 6') and is not mine to move, and moving the thing being measured is how a value set passes review and still ships wrong.

GDD 4.1, both shipping-slice bands now close on ascent, which is the finding that invalidated every other measurement last pass. Exhaust velocity is thrust_n / fuel_burn_kgs = 78000 / 26.0 = 3,000 m/s; wet mass is 1350 + 1800 = 3,150 kg; ideal dv = 3000 * ln(3150/1350) = 3000 * 0.8473 = 2,542 m/s against roughly 1,450 m/s to the suborbital band and roughly 1,800 m/s to the low band including circularisation, so the low band closes with about 40% margin and the suborbital band with about 75%, before counting the deorbit burn at roughly 100 m/s. Liftoff TWR is 78000 / (3150 * 9.0) = 2.75, up from the 1.65 the audit identified as the source of the gravity losses, which is where most of the gain actually comes from — the previous 1,750 kg ship had 1,605 m/s of ideal dv and was spending it hovering. fuel_tank tier 1 is now a range upgrade, not a required first purchase.

GDD 2.3.2, the parachute, stated as a canopy and not as a wish. Cd 1.8 over 870 m2 at the Researcher's rho0 = 1.5 and g = 9.0, against the flown full-hold mass of 1350 + 1397.8 = 2,747.8 kg: v = sqrt(2 * 2747.8 * 9.0 / (1.5 * 1.8 * 870)) = sqrt(49460.4 / 2349) = sqrt(21.056) = 4.59 m/s. That is the number in descent_speed_full_hold_ms, computed from the flown mass rather than an assumed one — the 0.85 m/s error the audit found was entirely the 1,599 kg assumption against a 2,247.8 kg ship, so this pass I derived the mass first and the canopy second. It sits under the 5.0 m/s soft line with 0.41 m/s of margin and above 3.5. Half hold is sqrt(2 * 2048.9 * 9.0 / 2349) = 3.96 m/s, and storage tier 1 at 8 slots is 3,213.7 kg giving 4.96 m/s — one slot inside the hard-landing line, which is exactly the crossing the Parachute upgrade is sold against. Parachute tier 1 at 1,180 m2 puts that 8-slot hold back at 4.26 m/s, and tier 2 at 1,500 m2 covers the 10-slot hold at 4.04 m/s. Storage and Parachute are a pair because the ladder is built as one.

GDD 2.3.1, the ablation optimum, rebuilt on the measured skim array. I adopted the audit's high-band measurement [1.0, 0.985, 0.971, 0.958] exactly, as the charter instructs — my [1.0, 0.851, 0.670, 0.411] claimed a 58.9% cooling where three skims actually removed 4.2%, and the flown array is the truth. Its last two steps are 0.014 and 0.013, so it saturates as the rule requires, and cycle_toll_growth stays at 1.8 > 1. Pricing it: three skims buy about 4.2% of peak, so the toll had to come down by roughly the same order or nothing could ever be worth flying. cycle_toll_base_pct drops 3.0 to 0.28, heat_cost_exponent goes to 3.0 (the heat term now has to be sensitive enough that a 1.5% peak reduction is worth more than a cycle) and heat_cost_coefficient to 1.25e-5, with skim_peak held at 22 so a skim's own heat cycle costs 1.25e-5 * 22^3 = 0.133 plate-percent. High band, evaluated term by term: heat terms 1.25e-5 * [138, 135.93, 133.998, 132.204]^3 = 32.85 / 31.39 / 30.08 / 28.88, tolls 0.28 * [1, 2.8, 6.04, 11.872] = 0.28 / 0.784 / 1.691 / 3.324, skim terms 0 / 0.133 / 0.266 / 0.399, totalling 33.13 / 32.31 / 32.03 / 32.61. Minimum at index 2, so optimal_skims.high = 2, inside the required 1-2. Low band totals 12.78 / 12.86 / 13.40 / 14.71 and suborbital 6.21 / 6.59 / 7.39 / 8.94, both minimal at 0, so no band exceeds the high band and the return leg does get harder with altitude. The margins are thin by construction — 0.28 plate-percent separates 1 skim from 2 in the high band, and 0.08 separates 0 from 1 in the low band — because a 1.5% cooling per skim cannot support a wide one. That thinness is the measurement's, not the tuning's.

GDD 2.3.1 pass count, the rule I cannot satisfy and am not going to fake. The audit's [cheapest_descent_is_multi_pass] check asks for a 2-4 committed-pass optimum, and its own evidence shows why no value in this file can produce one: braking altitude climbs with pass count inside a 43,000 m atmosphere, so extra passes brake in thinner air and peak heat is nearly flat in pass count (suborbital empty 70 to 74, high full hold 108 to 119). With peak heat flat, the heat term has nothing to give back and no assignment of the four ablation knobs moves the minimum off 1. The skim model above is the substitution the charter directs, and it does the anti-plunge job the GDD wanted — the cheapest high-band descent is genuinely not the direct entry — but it does it on skim count, not pass count. The remaining choice is a human's: substitute the skim framing into GDD 2.3.1, or take the GDD 4.5 risk-1 fallback of flat per-pass ablation with a hard pass cap. I have not tuned my way around a design pillar and the closest legal value set is the one above.

GDD 2.3.4, no shear under steady tow, proved as a bound rather than as a sample. Steady-state tension in a cable is m_piece * a, and a = jetpack_thrust / (suit_mass + total_towed), so tension = 240 * m_piece / (110 + total_towed), which is strictly below jetpack_thrust_n = 240 N for every load, at every tether count, for every piece in the catalog — adding mass suppresses acceleration faster than it adds weight to the cable. magnet_hold_force_n is 900 N at base tier, so the margin is at least 3.75x everywhere. The worst legal cases: two battery_pack_modules at 1,150 kg each give a = 240/2410 = 0.0996 m/s2 and 114.5 N per cable; a single cryo_propellant_sphere at 2,200 kg, the heaviest hand-tetherable piece in the game, gives a = 240/2310 = 0.1039 m/s2 and 228.6 N. Shear can therefore only fire on latch jerk and swing jerk, which is what the GDD says it is for.

GDD 2.3.6, a lazy run breaks even. launch_cost 120 is three suborbital smalls at size_class_base_value.small 40 * band_value_multiplier.suborbital 1.0, inside the stated two-to-three-cheap-pieces window. A lazy suborbital run that fills six crushed slots with four smalls and one medium sells for 4*40 + 90 = 250, against 120 for the stage and a direct suborbital entry's 6.21% of plate at replate_cost_per_pct 3 = 18.6, so 138.6 out and 250 in. It clears, and it clears by less than a single fragile piece at fragile_value_premium 3.0 (a suborbital fragile small is 120, half a run's gross on its own), which is the premium doing the job GDD 2.3.7 asks of it.

What I did not touch, so the next audit stays interpretable. heat_index stays at 78/100/138 — no check failed against it and the charter's normalisation (low direct entry reads about 100) is what it encodes. But the audit reports the simulator measuring the high-band direct entry at 161.5 peak, and if that figure is on the same normalised bar then heat_index.high is 17% low and should be routed as its own finding rather than folded into this pass. My cost_curve is internally consistent with 138; if the index moves to 161, the curve moves with it and I will re-emit both. Also untouched: cargo.base_slots, the whole reentry block, tow_fee, eva, and every economy value except none — the tow fee still runs zero inside 1,200 m and linearly to exactly 0.5 at half the planet's circumference of 628,319 m, never above 50% and never negative.

Consequential knock-on I am flagging rather than hiding: dry_mass_kg 1,350 is now well above the Researcher's assumed 1,800 kg staged-and-empty figure only after the stage is aboard, but it changes the ballistic coefficient of every descent in this file. Staged full hold at 2,747.8 kg over Cd 1.5 and 3.1 m2 gives beta = 2747.8 / 4.65 = 591 kg/m2, up from 483 at the old dry mass and above the Researcher's real-capsule band of 300-500. The atmosphere still brakes the ship, but less hard per pass than the baseline's drag ladder assumes, and rcs_thrust_n went 1200 to 1900 purely to keep rotational authority at the heavier mass rather than for any rule. If the Playtester finds the descents long, the cheapest lever is the Researcher's own suggestion — shield reference area at upgraded tiers, which is held at 3.1 m2 across every tier and cannot be right for a plate you pay to upgrade.
catalog_concerns: dented_pressure_bottle, mass_kg 380 in size_class small (1 crushed slot). It is the piece most responsible for the flown 232.96 kg per crushed slot, which is what forced dry_mass_kg from 850 to 1,350 to keep the GDD 2.3.5 doubling true. The catalog is self-consistent and I balanced against it as it stands, but the Designer should know that a 380 kg one-slot piece sets the per-slot mass of the whole shipping slice, and that the base ship's dry mass is now a function of it.

cryo_propellant_sphere, mass_kg 2200 in size_class medium, hand-tetherable. At base magnet_hold_force_n 900 N steady towing is safe by a wide margin (228.6 N), but latch jerk scales with closing speed times piece mass, so this piece defines the high band's shear behaviour on its own — it is 1.9x the next heaviest hand-tetherable piece. That is a sweep target rather than a defect, but if the Playtester finds latch jerk unforgiving at any magnet tier, this is the piece it will be about.
